alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 4 at 7:33AM EST until November 4 at 10:30AM EST by NWS Miami FL
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Broward County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1030 AM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 733 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Pembroke Pines, Miramar, Davie, Plantation, Sunrise, Weston,
Cooper City, Intersection I-75 And Griffin Road, Sunshine Acres,
Royal Palm Ranches, Pine Island Ridge, Nova Southeastern
University, Broadview Park, Markham Park and Downtown Davie.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/fl

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
700 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Western and Central Atlantic:
A broad area of low pressure is forming along a remnant frontal 
boundary a few hundred miles south of Bermuda. Environmental 
conditions could support this system gradually acquiring subtropical 
characteristics through this weekend while it moves slowly eastward 
over the western and central subtropical Atlantic. By early next 
week, environmental conditions are forecast to become unfavorable 
for further development. For more information on this system, 
including Gale Warnings, please see High Seas Forecasts issued by 
the National Weather Service. 
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
Forecaster Papin/Pasch
